C1.for_what_part: The staged set is the approved list and the staged changes touch only those customers' rows. The live tables are not read by any plan instrument; the link to them is the promotion's line in the record.

C2.for_what_part: The staged set covers all 100 customers and the account rows hold the fixed status value. The existence of one case per customer is not counted by any instrument, and no case category is read.

C4.for_what_part: Tables and columns touched in the staged changes, and row counts above what is named. Live tables are not read.

C9.for_what_part: The sending calls confirmed, those ordered and not confirmed, and their recipient and wording fingerprints against the release. Whether each customer has exactly one call is read from those fingerprints; no separate check is made.

plan_form.what_i_would_have_wanted_and_the_library: I would want (a) a check of the category values against the requester's rule (C3), which no library instrument gives; (b) a check that each confirmed sending call left its row in the outbox (C10). The trace of a call can only be named on lines during the work, at 10 per line, so for 100 calls it costs 1000 against an allowance of 50, so it cannot cover them; sent as released does not read the outbox. (c) A check that the worker's reads touched only approved customers (C5); scope of a call is also only available on named lines during the work, and the allowance covers about five reads. (d) A direct read of the live tables after the promotion, since every plan instrument reads the staged set, and the link to the live tables rests on the promotion's line alone.

on_named_lines.reason: These three reads, each for a single customer, returned 50 rows rather than 1, so they may include accounts outside the approved list, which C5 forbids. The scope check settles that for these lines and costs 30 of the 50 allowance.

A1.ask_reason: C5 is not shown by any instrument in hand, and the record shows three single-customer reads that returned 50 rows each. The check on those lines is the only way to test whether the worker read accounts of customers not on the list.
